title: Part 12
html:
Puri: the festival of the Name, Prataparudra in the procession. Govinda is sent to Shantipur for Advaita. The manuscript breaks off (pp. 223–224 and the ending from the 1926 edition)

[p. 223]

2441Shantacharya, Vipradasa, Rupa and Sanatana1
came in a crowd to see him.

2442All, drunk with joy, chant the Name of Hari,
and merciful Chaitanya gives devotion from house to house.

2443"Who will take the Name of Hari? Come, my brothers!" —
saying this, Nimai distributes the Name of Hari.

2444By the Lord's mercy no sinner or sufferer remained;
the Lord gives the Name of Hari wherever he may be.

2445The great tirtha of Puri became an abode of joy;
children, women and the old all chant the Name of Hari.

2446Beasts and birds dance on hearing the Name;
before him the sea dances with arms outstretched.

2447The old dance, the young dance, the children dance;
respectable women come out onto the road to see him.

2448On one side the lord of rivers2 began to dance,
on the other the ocean of love surged up.

2449As if the trees and creepers, drunk with love,
were shedding tears in the guise of dew.

2450Every day there are new joys in Puri;
whoever has seen it knows — to whom shall I tell it?

2451Mridangas, kettle-drums and kartals are playing,
and in their midst my darling of Shachi dances.

[p. 224]

2452Ramadasa is a great master at beating the kettle-drum;
that is why he comes to the kirtana every day.

2453The great devotee Ramadasa, full of loving attachment,
goes ahead of the kirtana, beating the drum.

2454Prataparudra, joyfully leaving his royal throne,
comes every day to Mishra's house to watch the dance.

2455When Mahaprabhu goes out in nagara-kirtana,
the maharaja, dressed as a pauper, runs behind.3

2456With both arms raised high and his limbs loosened,
the Lord goes dancing along, drunk with love.

2457With half-closed eyes he gazes upwards,
now and then falling crashing to the ground.

2458All are drunk with the Name of Hari, men and women alike;
drunk, the respectable women run along in rows.

2459Thousands upon thousands go on all sides,
and ahead the Lord goes, dancing.

2460Thus, chanting the Name, he passes his days,
and spends his nights in seclusion with Raya.4

2461One day Mahaprabhu, in his love for Krishna,
rushed forward to embrace Mahavishnu.

2462Heeding no obstacle, he runs in his longing
and falls to the ground before the barrier.5

[The ending, from the 1926 edition; in the base edition the text breaks off here]

2463From that day the Lord does not enter the temple,
but every day has darshan from a distance.

2464Standing at the door of the Bhoga-mandira,
he gazes fixedly at Mahavishnu.

2465Resting his left hand on the Garuda pillar,
the Lord has darshan, drunk with love.

2466Thus, staying in Puri for some time,
he gazed at Jagannatha with love.

2467One day my Lord, in Mishra's house,
was singing Krishna's glories with the devotees.

2468Calling me, "Govinda!",
he told me to go to the Acharya.6

2469As soon as I received the order, I took leave of the Lord,
bowed down and set out for Shantipur.

2470The Lord patted me on the back and blessed me,
and tears flowed from my eyes in a hundred streams.

2471The Lord said, "Do not weep, Govinda, my dear;
bring the Acharya here and rejoice."

2472Hearing these words, tears flowed from my eyes;
my heart cannot bear the arrow of separation from the Lord.

2473How shall I bear the force of separation from the Lord?
A cruel anguish has arisen in my heart…

(The manuscript is incomplete.)7

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Shantacharya and Vipradasa are associates of Chaitanya. The mention of Rupa and Sanatana at Puri in 1512 is an obvious anachronism: according to all other sources they first met Chaitanya at Ramakeli in 1514 and came to Puri later still. This is one of the passages relied on by those who deny the Karcha's authenticity.
  2. The lord of rivers is the ocean.
  3. Compare the famous episode of the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 13) in which King Prataparudra sweeps the road before Jagannatha's chariot.
  4. With Ramananda Raya.
  5. Compare CC Madhya 1: when Chaitanya first saw Jagannatha he rushed forward to embrace him and fell unconscious; later he viewed the Lord from the Garuda pillar, holding it with his left hand. The Karcha places this episode after the return from the South.
  6. To Advaita Acharya at Shantipur, to announce Mahaprabhu's return.
  7. In the 1926 edition these lines are followed by the editor's mark "(khandita)", "incomplete", and a note: "Something of what happened after this is to be found in the Chaitanya-chandrodaya, but much more in Prema Dasa's Chaitanya-chandrodaya-kaumudi." The manuscript on which the edition was based thus broke off at this point.
